newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo H1 industry growth seen at 6 pct - Institute.
newsitem.headline: Yugo H1 industry growth seen at 6 pct - Institute.

text.p: Yugoslavia's industry will grow six percent in the first half of 1997, but that is not enough to bring the country back to its pre-1990 levels, Belgrade-based Economics Institute said in its latest report.

"A six percent output growth over the same period 1996 is good if compared to other transition economies but insufficient to return this industry to its pre-sanctions level," said Goran Pitic, an economist with the institute.
Three and a half years of war-related U.N. sanctions against Yugoslavia and economic mismanagement brought the country's industry to a virtual standstill.
Output has been on an upward trend since sanctions were lifted last October, but experts attributed this mainly to a low start base.

Month-on-month industrial output grew 7.4 percent in March, 11.4 percent in February but was 20.8 percent down in January. Year-on-year March output stood at 9.2. Cumulative January-March output grew 6.3 percent over the same period 1996.
The 1997 output growth rate is officially forecast at 14 percent.
But lack of working capital remains a major obstacle to any industrial growth.

"Fresh working capital is needed to substantially change the structure of the industry and attract fresh funds so that the country embarks on structural reforms," said Miroljub Labus another economist with the institute.
Economists also cautioned that Yugoslavia's industry output growth could slow down in several months time if imports of raw material declines.
Analysts expect imports growth to falter on shortage of funds and the industry to feel ill-effects of reduced raw material imports in three to four months.
"This means that some time late in summer or early autumn industries will begin to feel shortage of imported raw materials," he said. -- Beti Blilandzic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
